title: Developer Uses AI to Clone Adobe Apps, Claims 'Software Is Over'
title_zh: 开发者用AI克隆Adobe软件，宣称“软件时代结束了”
lead: A software developer has used an AI model to build free, open-source versions of Adobe's most popular creative tools. He promises they will soon match Adobe's features exactly, though experts and users have doubts.
lead_zh: 一位软件开发者利用AI模型制作了Adobe最受欢迎创意工具的自由开源版本。他承诺这些工具很快就能完全比肩Adobe，但专家和用户对此表示怀疑。

preview_zh: 多年来，想避开Adobe昂贵Creative Suite的人可以选择几款免费或开源的替代品。如今，一位名叫Brandon Thomas的开发者正利用AI驱动的逆向工程，复制Adobe知名软件的外观、感觉和功能。他的目标是尽快达到他所说的“完美保真度”。
paragraphs: For years, people who wanted to avoid Adobe's expensive Creative Suite could choose from several free or open-source alternatives. Now, a developer named Brandon Thomas is using AI-powered reverse engineering to copy the look, feel, and functions of Adobe's well-known software. His goal is to achieve what he calls 'perfect fidelity' as soon as possible.

Artcraft, which began last year as a controllable AI tool for artists, has now pivoted to a suite of seven open-source apps. These recreate the interfaces and tools found in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. Thomas said he used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 to create 'clean-room replacements' for Adobe's closed-source software, written in Rust and available for browsers via WebAssembly.

While commenters on Reddit and Hacker News have pointed out many current shortcomings, Thomas has made bold promises. He initially said the apps would reach '100% feature parity within a month,' but later adjusted that to '99% parity will take a while, but I'm sure it'll be measured in months and not years.' The software is currently in a 'super early alpha' state.

Thomas, who has about a decade of experience with large-scale Rust projects, said he was inspired to build these alternatives after being 'bit by the dark pattern cancellation fee one too many times.' The apps are totally free under MIT/Apache licenses, and development is funded by selling token-based access to the pre-existing Artcraft visual AI model and IDE.

This is the latest example of coders using AI to speed up reverse engineering, a long-standing but labor-intensive practice that is generally considered legal. However, the Artcraft apps could still face legal trouble if their 'trade dress' too closely mimics Adobe's familiar appearance and interface.

After coding exclusively with AI tools since February, Thomas foresees a near future when everyday developers can re-create open-source versions of popular paid software. He wrote, 'We'll replace Google Search, we'll build our own smartphones, we'll build better infra. We'll remove all the ads and de-enshittify the entire tech world.' In an earlier comment, he gloated, 'Software is over,' claiming to have 'one-shotted Photoshop. The whole thing.'
paragraphs_zh: 多年来，想避开Adobe昂贵Creative Suite的人可以选择几款免费或开源的替代品。如今，一位名叫Brandon Thomas的开发者正利用AI驱动的逆向工程，复制Adobe知名软件的外观、感觉和功能。他的目标是尽快达到他所说的“完美保真度”。

Artcraft去年最初是一款面向艺术家的可控AI工具，现已转型为一套包含七款开源应用的软件套件。这些应用重现了Photoshop、Illustrator、Premiere、Lightroom、After Effects、InDesign和Acrobat Pro中的界面和工具。Thomas表示，他使用Anthropic的Claude Opus 5.5为Adobe的闭源软件创建了“洁净室替代品”，用Rust编写，并通过WebAssembly在浏览器中可用。
虽然Reddit和Hacker News上的评论者指出了当前许多不足之处，但Thomas做出了大胆承诺。他最初称这些应用将在“一个月内达到100%功能对等”，但后来调整为“99%的对等还需要一段时间，但我确信会以月而非年来衡量。”该软件目前处于“超级早期alpha”阶段。
Thomas在大型Rust项目方面有约十年经验，他说自己是因为“被暗黑模式的取消费坑了太多次”才受到启发，开始构建这些替代品。这些应用在MIT/Apache许可下完全免费，开发资金来自销售对现有Artcraft视觉AI模型和IDE的基于代币的访问权限。
这是程序员利用AI加速逆向工程的最新例子。逆向工程是一种长期存在但劳动密集的做法，通常被认为合法。然而，如果Artcraft应用的外观和界面与Adobe过于相似，仍可能因“商业外观”问题面临法律麻烦。
自二月以来完全使用AI工具编程后，Thomas预见在不久的将来，普通开发者也能重新创建流行付费软件的开源版本。他写道：“我们将取代谷歌搜索，我们将制造自己的智能手机，我们将建设更好的基础设施。我们将移除所有广告，让整个科技世界去屎化。”在早些时候的评论中，他得意地说：“软件时代结束了”，并声称“一击即中Photoshop。整个东西。”

For a while, those hoping to
avoid the difficulty and expense of dealing with Adobe’s Creative Suite
have been able to use
several free and/or open-source alternatives
that replicate some or all of those capabilities. Now, one developer is using AI-powered reverse engineering to mimic the look, feel, and functionality of Adobe’s well-known software with what he hopes will soon be perfect fidelity.
Artcraft
got its start
last year
as a “controllable AI for artists” that allows for precise post-generation editing of AI-crafted images and videos. Over the weekend, though, the brand
debuted its pivot
to
a suite of seven open source apps
recreating the user interface and tools found in Adobe’s Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro.
In
announcing those new apps on Reddit
earlier this week,
software developer Brandon Thomas
said he used Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 to create “clean-room replacements” for Adobe’s closed source software in Rust (with WebAssembly versions available for use in a browser). And while commenters
on Hacker News
and
elsewhere
have
taken pains
to point out the new software’s many current shortcomings, Thomas make the grandiose promise that
the current “super early alpha” state
will soon lead to something just as functional as anything Adobe has ever put out.
“We’re going to reach 100% [feature] parity within a month,” Thomas
stated on Reddit
of his plans to quickly squash bugs and add features with the help of community reports. Days later,
on Hacker News
, he amended that position slightly to say that “99% parity will take a while, but I’m sure it’ll be measured in months and not years.”
Is software over?
Thomas, who says he has about a decade of experience working on large-scale Rust projects,
wrote on Hacker News
that he was inspired to create his own open source Adobe software alternatives after being “bit by the dark pattern ‘cancellation fee’ one too many times.” Development of the totally free options offered here under MIT/Apache licenses will be funded, Thomas
wrote
, by selling token-based access to
the pre-existing Artcraft visual AI model and IDE
, which is offered as an imagery-generation option inside the apps alongside third-party models. This revenue stream will help ensure these apps aren’t “going to be some orphaned small-team project,” Thomas wrote. “We have a team building popular software for filmmakers, so supporting this is fully funded.”
Thomas is the
latest in a long line
of coders using AI tools to speed up the
long-standing but labor-intensive practice
of reverse engineering (i.e., replicating the functionality of a piece of software without directly copying the code itself). While that practice has
generally been found legally acceptable
, the ArtCraft apps
could still face legal trouble
if their “trade dress” too closely mimics Adobe’s familiar appearance and interface.
After coding exclusively with AI tools since February, Thomas
said
he foresees a near future when everyday developers can re-create open source versions of popular paid software to “take back the internet and own tech forever.”
“Now you can just create 1:1 functional equivalents, clean room, that are highly performant and cross-platform. Nothing is stopping you,” Thomas wrote. “We’ll replace Google Search, we’ll build our own smartphones, we’ll build better infra. We’ll remove all the ads and de-enshittify the entire tech world.”
“Software is over,” he gloated in
an earlier comment
, claiming to have “one-shotted Photoshop. The whole thing.”
